$comment: The one home for every number and enum a Refract rule enforces. Rules cite the id (THR-…) instead of restating the value; scripts/lint-rule-literals.sh fails a NEW numeric literal in a MUST rule that does not cite one (ratchet). JSON, not YAML: the consumers are python3 standard-library scripts (gate-check.py, standards-check.py, the lints) and the model; nothing in a user's repo parses YAML, and a hand-rolled YAML subset fails silently — the same reason .claude/gates.json is JSON. A project overrides a value in .claude/thresholds.local.json with the same id; an override may TIGHTEN a floor ("floor": true) and never loosen it (templates/governance/precedence.md § 2). Each entry: value (number, string or object), unit, floor (true = a project may only tighten), owner (the catalog row or rule that applies it), why.

THR-RES-TIMEOUT.why: an external call with no timeout cascades; 2 s is a default for in-region calls, never a ceiling the caller's own budget cannot fit

never_on: a non-idempotent write without an idempotency key

THR-RES-RETRY.why: 429 is a back-off signal, not a terminal 4xx: retry it no sooner than Retry-After (precedence A7); unbounded attempts turn a provider storm into a bill or a ban

value.floor: exact decimal DECIMAL(p,s) or integer minor units, always with a currency; never float

THR-MONEY.why: DATA-9 is the floor; inside the payment and ledger domains integer minor units win (precedence A14)

THR-ERR-ENVELOPE.why: one envelope mapped in one place; public APIs document it as their contract

THR-PAGINATION.why: every list has a default and a hard maximum; offset past ~1000 rescans rows on most engines

THR-PASSWORD-HASH.why: the algorithm name is not the control, the parameters are (OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet minimums)

THR-TOKEN-TTL.why: short-lived credentials bound the blast radius of a leak

THR-CACHE-TTL.why: an explicit TTL with jitter avoids a synchronized expiry stampede

THR-PERF-REGRESSION.why: a delta inside the noise band is NO-CHANGE; a measured regression past the threshold is a FAIL unless waived

value.changed_lines: ratchet — never below the project's declared floor

THR-COVERAGE.why: a ratchet, not a magic number: the project declares the floor

THR-MUTATION.why: diff-scoped mutation proves the tests would notice the change being wrong

THR-NIT-CAP.why: more nits bury the Important findings; after round 1 only Important findings post

THR-LOOP.why: a third non-converging pass is an upstream problem; escalate to a human with the ledger

THR-WAIVER.why: an expired waiver is a FAIL

THR-FN-LEN.owner: the project's linter config (max-lines-per-function / funlen / PLR0915 / …)
THR-FN-LEN.why: there is no portable function-length number; the project's configured linter value is the rule (precedence A5). With no linter configured the length rule is advisory, never a hard FAIL

THR-COMPLEXITY.why: same as THR-FN-LEN: read the configured value; a change may not raise it beyond the touched file's baseline

THR-DRY.why: a second copy of something that already exists reuses it; a NEW shared abstraction waits for the third occurrence (precedence A28)

THR-ARCH-RELATIVE.unit: percentile of this repo's own distribution
THR-ARCH-RELATIVE.owner: code-quality architectural-diagnosis § 3, § 4, § 9 (triage cut-offs, never findings alone — precedents/code-quality.md § 51)
THR-ARCH-RELATIVE.why: fixed cut-offs (in-degree >= 30, >= 500 LOC) flagged 458 files on a real monorepo, mostly its shared kernel and composition roots; a cut at the repo's own percentiles (Alves et al., ICSM 2010) ranks against what is normal here. A module is a candidate above the fan-in, fan-out or LOC percentile; a function is a hotspot at or above the churn AND complexity percentiles; an SDP edge needs the depended-on module to be less stable by the delta. A project value in .claude/thresholds.local.json wins

THR-TODO.why: an owner and a date make a TODO expire; a ticket alone does not (precedence A2)

THR-LOG-LEVEL.why: a recovered catch logs at warn so the recovery is visible in production (precedence A9); a client error (404, validation) is the caller's mistake and logs at warn or below, a server error logs at error, once per request

THR-CLAUDE-MD-LINES.why: code.claude.com memory docs: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; longer files cost context and reduce adherence

THR-ALWAYS-ON-TOKENS.why: always-on rules and CLAUDE.md are paid on every turn before the user types

THR-DESC-BUDGET.why: descriptions are routing text paid before anyone asks; over the platform budget descriptions are truncated to names

value.axe_gate: no new serious or critical violation vs the baseline, per touched route-state

THR-A11Y.owner: governance/engineering-baseline/web.md WEB-8 · mobile.md MOB-7 · frontend a11y-scan (axe_gate, gate G9) · ui-ux ux-reviewer
THR-A11Y.why: the platform guidelines' minimums; 24×24 CSS px is SC 2.5.8 (AA) and 44×44 the house target (2.5.5 is AAA). axe_gate replaces a Lighthouse accessibility score: a score is not axe and not conformance, and a baseline diff is the only automated a11y result a change can fail

THR-UI-STATES.owner: ui-ux state-matrix (state-matrix-lint.py, gate G12 state-matrix) · ui-state-scan
THR-UI-STATES.why: every UI surface has a row for every required state, written or n-a with a reason; a conditional state is required where the surface has the trigger (a write, a delete, a detail route, a form). A project may ADD states in .claude/thresholds.local.json, never drop a required one

value.measure: brotli bytes of the entry closure a route loads, production build
value.no_budget: report-flagged (declare a budget), never OVER BUDGET

THR-WEB-BUNDLE.why: one default where bundle-analyze and /bundle-perf said 150 KB brotli and /audit --target-bundle said 250 KB: a working default for an interactive app on a mid-tier mobile connection, not an industry constant. A budget the project declared (ai/runtime/perf-budgets.md, size-limit, lighthouserc) wins outright

THR-LHCI.why: a single Lighthouse run is not a measurement; the median of five runs against the production build is, and every numeric assertion reads the median run

accepted_sets.pyrra: 14/7/2/1, windows scaled to the SLO period (28d)

THR-OBS-BURN.why: the literal is the review defect, the arithmetic is the rule: a hard-coded 14.4 marks every Pyrra rule (14/7/2/1 on 28d) and the Workbook's own 4th 3× 24h/2h tier (sloth google-30d) as wrong. A factor is a finding only when it fails the formula for the declared objective and period

THR-OBS-RATE-WINDOW.unit: multiple of the job's scrape interval
THR-OBS-RATE-WINDOW.why: a rate window under 2× the scrape interval can hold fewer than two samples and returns nothing; on Prometheus 3 range selectors are left-open, so exactly 1× is empty. 2–4× is style, not a bug

value.severity_vocab_override: project may replace the vocabulary with the one its Alertmanager routes use

THR-OBS-ALERT.owner: packs/observability/skills/alert-rule-lint §1, §2, §8 (AL-02, AL-03, AM-04) · /obs-fix reward-hack grep (for raised past page_for_max)
THR-OBS-ALERT.why: a page that waits 30m before firing has spent the incident; a pager route that groups for over 5m delays the first page; a repeat under 30m is noise. The severity vocabulary is whatever the routes match on, so a project override names its own, never none

THR-OBS-CARDINALITY.owner: packs/observability/skills/metric-hygiene-scan §1 · telemetry-config-scan §4 (MT-01, PL-04, PL-08) · finops prices the series
THR-OBS-CARDINALITY.why: series = ∏ distinct label values × replicas; past ~10 values a label is a design question and past ~100 an investigation, and an unbounded value (id, raw path, email, trace id) is a TSDB outage risk. Loki labels index streams: keep dynamic labels to tens of values and the rest in the line

THR-OBS-PAGE-BUDGET.owner: packs/observability/commands/alert-design.md Phase 6 · sre-engineer · alert-audit (noise, against fire history)
THR-OBS-PAGE-BUDGET.why: moved from alert-design so the number has one home: each page costs follow-up time (postmortem, fix, review), so a 12h shift absorbs about two pages before on-call stops fixing causes. Judged against fire history, else NO-DATA
